en.html:
Muramasa screamed. My entire state of mind she had spoken for me.

That gravitational barrier Hikaru called her shield must be equivalent to our magnetic barrier—negative-pole magnetic armor. That she could use one, nothing surprising about that.

But fighting with it up ALL THE TIME—

An enormous amount of heat Muramasa's magnetic barrier consumed. Keep it up, and very little power was left for flight or anything else.

Normally we judged the exact instant an attack would strike. For that instant only, put the barrier up.

Leave it up continuously? Any surprise attack could be met, haan. In exchange, the armor's performance would fall through the floor. Reduced fighting ability, forget that—even flying properly would probably become impossible.

Aur madam? Madam had kept the whole thing wrapped around herself and carried on. All our desperate fighting, and from her side it was merely a little activity done without taking the blanket off. Thand lag jayegi, perhaps. Must not catch a chill while humiliating Kageaki.

No. Such a thought was nonsense. The actual explanation was worse than the nonsense.

Matlab.

ja.html:
村正の悲鳴は、俺の心境を丸々代弁していた。

　光の言う<ruby>辰気障壁<rt>たて</rt></ruby>とは、<ruby>村正<rt>おれたち</rt></ruby>の用いる磁気障壁――
負極の磁装と同等のものだろう。
　それが使えること自体は、何ら驚くに値しない。

　しかし。
　常に障壁を張り巡らせながら戦っていた、となると
――

　村正の磁気障壁は多大な熱量を必要とする。
　従って障壁の展開中は、騎航その他の機能に割ける
余力が極めて少なくなる。

　ために通常、磁気障壁は敵騎の攻撃を浴びる一瞬を
見切ってその間のみ展開することになる。

　もしもこれを常時張れば、敵手がどう不意を打って
きても対応できる代わり、騎体性能が激減する。
　総じて戦闘能力は低下する――どころではなく騎航
すらまともに行えなくなるだろう。

　<ruby>つまり<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>。

en.html:
Nothing I could see.

Nothing I could understand.

...Aise kaise? How was this possible?

Silver Star's attacks had always been overwhelmingly fast. Even so, reaction might fail me, but when an attack came, at least I could recognize it.

That I had been attacked, this much I could understand.

...Now even this facility was gone.

When did she hit me? From where? HOW?
Afterwards also, trying to look back, not a thing made sense.

————What kind of bloody impossibility was THIS!!

en.html:
Kan. Direct apprehension.

An awareness said to exist beyond the senses. See light, then understand; hear a sound, then understand—no need for all these roundabout steps. Apprehend the fight ITSELF. Respond to that.

Not merely strong. Not merely skillful.
Beyond even those praised as masters, as experts.

Only a warrior who had come to be called a sword saint possessed such a thing.

...Naturally, I would not have it. Why would I have it?
But.

Without something like that, what bloody contest could there be!
